This notebook uses one small feature matrix to make shapes and core
linear-algebra operations visible. Run the cells from top to bottom.

## Load the shared fixture

The helper keeps file loading and plot construction out of the learning flow.
Every numerical operation below uses base R directly; ggplot2 is used only for
the diagram.

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
source("r_helpers.R")

tables <- load_fixture_tables()
feature_names <- names(tables$features)[-1]
coefficient_names <- as.character(tables$coefficients$feature)
stopifnot(identical(coefficient_names, feature_names))

X <- as.matrix(tables$features[, feature_names, drop = FALSE])
storage.mode(X) <- "double"
beta <- as.double(tables$coefficients$coefficient)
A <- as.matrix(tables$system[, c("a1", "a2"), drop = FALSE])
storage.mode(A) <- "double"
b <- as.double(tables$system$b)
expected <- setNames(
  as.double(tables$expected$value),
  tables$expected$name
)
```

## Inspect shapes

`X` has three observations and two features. `beta` has one coefficient for
each feature, so `X %*% beta` is valid.

```{r}
cat("feature order:", paste(feature_names, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("X: shape =", paste(dim(X), collapse = " x "), ", type =", typeof(X), "\n")
cat("beta: length =", length(beta), ", type =", typeof(beta), "\n")
cat("t(X): shape =", paste(dim(t(X)), collapse = " x "), "\n")

X
beta
```

## Multiply a matrix by a vector

The matching inner dimensions disappear. The outer dimension—three
observations—determines the three prediction values.

```{r}
#| label: fig-matrix-multiplication
#| fig-cap: "The two inner dimensions match, so each observation receives one dot-product result."
#| fig-alt: "A three-by-two feature matrix multiplied by a two-value coefficient vector produces three predictions; every cell and dimension is labeled."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
predictions <- drop(X %*% beta)
matrix_multiplication_plot(X, beta, predictions)
```

## Compute the core operations

A dot product produces one number, a norm measures vector length, and
`crossprod(X)` compares every feature with every feature. The final expression
solves a separate two-equation system.

```{r}
first_row_dot <- drop(X[1, ] %*% beta)
coefficient_norm <- sqrt(sum(beta^2))
gram_matrix <- crossprod(X)
system_solution <- solve(A, b)

cat("first row dot beta:", first_row_dot, "\n")
cat("beta norm:", sprintf("%.12f", coefficient_norm), "\n")
cat("predictions:", paste(predictions, collapse = ", "), "\n")
gram_matrix
cat("linear-system solution:", paste(system_solution, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

Check the results against the same reference values used by the Python
notebooks.

```{r}
expected_predictions <- expected[paste0("prediction_", 1:3)]
expected_gram <- matrix(
  expected[c("gram_11", "gram_21", "gram_12", "gram_22")],
  nrow = 2,
  ncol = 2
)
expected_solution <- expected[c("solution_1", "solution_2")]

assert_close(first_row_dot, expected[["first_row_dot"]], "first-row dot product")
assert_close(coefficient_norm, expected[["coefficient_norm"]], "coefficient norm")
assert_close(predictions, expected_predictions, "predictions")
assert_close(gram_matrix, expected_gram, "Gram matrix")
assert_close(system_solution, expected_solution, "linear-system solution")
cat("The base R results match the shared reference.\n")
```

## Recycling and shape errors

Base R recycles a vector down a matrix's column-major storage. That is not the
same as adding one value to each feature column, so `sweep()` makes the intended
operation explicit. Matrix multiplication is stricter: a length-three
coefficient vector is incompatible with the two columns of `X`.

```{r}
recycled_sum <- X + beta
columnwise_sum <- sweep(X, MARGIN = 2, STATS = beta, FUN = "+")
expected_columnwise_sum <- matrix(
  c(1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 1.0, 3.0, 5.0),
  nrow = 3,
  ncol = 2
)
assert_close(columnwise_sum, expected_columnwise_sum, "explicit column addition")

recycled_sum
columnwise_sum
```

```{r}
invalid_shape_message <- tryCatch(
  {
    X %*% c(beta, 2.0)
    ""
  },
  error = conditionMessage
)

stopifnot(nzchar(invalid_shape_message))
cat("Expected incompatible-shape error:", invalid_shape_message, "\n")
cat("All T02 base R checks passed.\n")
```
